answer: The course 'Essentials of Global Health' is offered by Yale University on Coursera (https://www.coursera.org/learn/essentials-global-health). Its instructor is Richard Skolnik, former Lecturer at the Yale School of Public Health and Yale School of Management. Bio summary: Richard Skolnik has more than 40 years of experience in international development and global health and is the author of the widely used textbook 'Global Health 101' (3rd edition). He spent 25 years at the World Bank, retiring as Director for Health and Education for the South Asia Region, with health work spanning West Africa, the Middle East and North Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, and South Asia, focused on health systems financing, equity, maternal and child health, and control of communicable diseases. After the World Bank he was Vice President for International Programs at PRB and Director of the Center for Global Health at The George Washington University, where he taught undergraduate global health for 8 years; he also served as Executive Director of the Harvard PEPFAR program for AIDS treatment in Botswana, Nigeria, and Tanzania. He has served on the Global Fund's Technical Review Panel, WHO advisory groups, and was deeply involved in establishing STOP TB; more recently he reviewed HIV financing in India, Cambodia, and Nigeria with the Results for Development Institute, and serves on the editorial advisory bodies of DCP3 and Millions Saved. He holds a BA from Yale University and an MPA from Princeton University's Woodrow Wilson School. Additional courses: Richard Skolnik offers no additional courses on Coursera; his instructor profile's 'Courses - English' section lists only 'Essentials of Global Health'.
